findings.question: Q5 ACHIEVE-3 design
findings.statement: ACHIEVE-3 was a 52-week, randomised, open-label, active-controlled, multicentre, multinational phase 3 trial in adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin (>=1500 mg/day), HbA1c 7.0-10.5%, BMI >=25, at 131 centres in Argentina, China, Japan, Mexico and the USA.

findings.statement: ACHIEVE-3 randomized 1698 participants 1:1:1:1 to orforglipron 12 mg (n=424) or 36 mg (n=423) or oral semaglutide 7 mg (n=426) or 14 mg (n=425), all once daily.

findings.locator_quote: 401 were randomly assigned to three groups (3 mg, n=132; 12 mg, n=135; and 36 mg, n=134)
findings.notes: Peer-reviewed. Discontinuations due to an adverse event: 5% (3 mg), 8% (12 mg), 14% (36 mg) per abstract.

findings.question: Q7 other phase 3 trials
findings.statement: Registry snapshot (2026-10-13): 27 interventional Phase 3 orforglipron studies are listed; ongoing examples include the cardiovascular outcomes trial ATTAIN-Outcomes (NCT07241390, recruiting, planned enrollment 7140, primary completion 2031-08) and ATTAIN-OSA (NCT06649045, status completed, primary completion 2026-07-21, no results posted).
findings.notes: Other records: ATTAIN-J NCT05931380 (completed, results posted; regional trial reviewed by FDA as supporting data), ACHIEVE-PEDS NCT07668336 vs dulaglutide in pediatric type 2 diabetes (not yet recruiting), ATTAIN-PAD NCT07223593, ATTAIN-OA PAIN NCT07153471, ATTAIN-NOW NCT07794579, RESTRAIN-SUI NCT07202884, ATTAIN-Hypertension master protocol NCT06948422.

findings.question: Q7 other phase 3 trials
findings.statement: Head-to-head (active-comparator) phase 3 trials of orforglipron identified: ACHIEVE-3 vs oral semaglutide 7/14 mg, ACHIEVE-2 vs dapagliflozin 10 mg, ACHIEVE-4 vs insulin glargine (all completed and published), and ACHIEVE-PEDS vs dulaglutide (not yet recruiting). No completed head-to-head trial against an injectable GLP-1/GIP agonist for weight management was found.
findings.notes: A published population-adjusted indirect comparison versus oral semaglutide 25 mg exists (PMID 42225305) but is not a randomized head-to-head trial.

not_found: Journal full texts: NEJM (ATTAIN-1) and Lancet (ATTAIN-2, ACHIEVE-3, ACHIEVE-4) full-text pages returned HTTP 403 and none of the four is in PMC/Europe PMC; only PubMed abstracts were used. Consequently per-arm efficacy-estimand confidence intervals from the journals were not retrieved (efficacy-estimand point estimates come from Lilly releases; registry on-treatment estimates with CIs for differences are recorded with estimand = not_stated).

ACHIEVE-4 hazard ratios for individual MACE components other than cardiovascular death (non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, hospitalisation for unstable angina): not found in the PubMed abstract, the two Lilly releases, Lilly Medical Information, or the registry (no results posted).

ACHIEVE-4 testing hierarchy: whether superiority for MACE-4 and/or MACE-3 was formally prespecified and multiplicity-controlled could not be confirmed (Lancet full text, supplement, protocol and SAP not accessible; ClinicalTrials.gov has no documents or results for NCT05803421). Only the non-inferiority criterion (upper two-sided 95% CI limit < 1.8) is documented.

ACHIEVE-4 per-term gastrointestinal adverse-event percentages (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea) per arm, and the insulin glargine arm's rate of treatment discontinuation due to adverse events: not found (only overall GI AE incidence per arm and the orforglipron 10.6% discontinuation figure).
ACHIEVE-4 treatment-regimen-estimand HbA1c and body-weight results: not found; releases report the efficacy estimand only.

ATTAIN-2 proportion achieving >=20% weight reduction under the efficacy estimand, and treatment-regimen >=20% values from the publication: not found (only the label's ITT values 0.7/2.6/4.4/10.8%, which the label marks as not controlled for multiplicity).

A capsule-to-tablet mapping stated in the prescribing information itself: not present. The label only says the trials used an 'investigational orforglipron formulation' shown as 'equivalent dosages'; the explicit mapping (1/3/6/12/24/36 mg capsule = 0.8/2.5/5.5/9/14.5/17.2 mg tablet) is documented in the FDA multidisciplinary review, the bioequivalence publication, the registry record NCT06440980 and Lilly materials.

Any clinical efficacy or safety trial conducted with the marketed tablet in the phase 3 program: none found; FDA states the tablet review relied on bioequivalence. (Note: per-capsule-strength composition or why capsule and tablet bioavailability differ beyond 'difference in drug absorption' was not found.)

FDA action, acceptance/filing date or goal date for the US type 2 diabetes submission: not found; only Lilly's statement that the submission was made (Q2 2026 release). The FDA label and Drugs@FDA show no type 2 diabetes indication as of 2026-10-13.

EU: no CHMP opinion or European Commission decision for orforglipron found (CHMP May 2026 agenda shows list-of-questions stage; September 2026 CHMP highlights do not mention it; EMA product pages for 'foundayo' returned 403/404). October 2026 CHMP outcome, if any, was not yet published on the retrieval date.
investor.lilly.com press-release pages and the SEC EDGAR copy of the Q2 2026 release returned HTTP 403; the PR Newswire copies of the same Lilly releases were used instead and are cited as the URLs.
The date printed on the FDA approval letter could not be extracted from the PDF text; the approval date 2026-04-01 is taken from Drugs@FDA.
UK SmPC text and exact UK indication wording: not retrieved (only the MHRA press release).
Status in other jurisdictions (e.g. Japan, China, Canada): not searched in depth; only Lilly's statement of submissions in more than 40 countries.
conflicts: ATTAIN-1 treatment-regimen weight change differs slightly by source: NEJM abstract -7.5/-8.4/-11.2% (6/12/36 mg) vs placebo -2.1%; FDA label Table 6 -7.4/-8.3/-11.1% vs -2.1%; FDA reviewer's analysis -7.4/-8.3/-11.2% vs -2.1%. Differences vs placebo: Lilly Medical Information citing NEJM -5.5 (-6.5,-4.5), -6.3 (-7.3,-5.4), -9.1 (-10.1,-8.1); label -5.3 (-6.1,-4.4), -6.2 (-7.1,-5.3), -9 (-10,-8.1); FDA review -5.3 (-6.1,-4.5), -6.2 (-7.1,-5.3), -9.0 (-10.0,-8.1). Likely different missing-data imputation (label/FDA: 'modified multiple imputation'); all are labelled treatment-regimen/ITT.

ATTAIN-1 treatment-regimen responder rates differ between publication/release and label: >=5% 60.6/63.5/71.8 vs placebo 26.8 (release) versus 59.6/63.1/71.5 vs 26.8 (label); >=10% 33.3/40.0/54.6 vs 12.9 versus 32.5/39.8/54.5 vs 13; >=15% 15.1/20.3/36.0 vs 5.9 versus 14.3/20.1/35.9 vs 6; >=20% 6.4/9.0/18.4 vs 2.8 versus 5.9/8.9/18.4 vs 2.9.

ATTAIN-1 treatment discontinuation due to adverse events: topline release (2025-08-07) 5.1/7.7/10.3% vs placebo 2.6%; NEJM abstract and the 2025-09-16 release 5.3/7.9/10.3% vs 2.7%. FDA label (pooled with ATTAIN-2) rounds to 6/9/10% vs 3%.

ATTAIN-2 treatment discontinuation due to adverse events: Lancet abstract 6.1-9.9% (orforglipron) vs 4.1% (placebo); Lilly topline release and Lilly Medical Information table 6.1/10.6/10.6% vs 4.6%. The Lilly Medical page shows both sets (text vs table), implying different derivations (disposition reason vs adverse-event listing).

ATTAIN-2 treatment-regimen estimates: Lancet abstract ETD -2.7 (-3.7 to -1.6) for 6 mg and -7.1 (-8.2 to -6.1) for 36 mg versus label/FDA review -2.6 (-3.5, -1.6) and -7.1 (-8.1, -6.1); responder rates in company sources (>=5% 47.7/54.6/67.2 vs 26.6; >=10% 22.6/31.2/45.6 vs 9.0; >=15% 6.8/14.4/26.0 vs 3.0) versus label (47.4/54.7/67 vs 26.8; 22.5/31.1/45.6 vs 9.2; 6.7/14.4/25.9 vs 3.1).

Dose labelling of identical trial arms differs by source and date: journals, registry and 2025/early-2026 releases use investigational capsule doses (3, 6, 12, 36 mg); the FDA label, Lilly Medical Information and releases from June 2026 use tablet-equivalent dosages (2.5, 5.5, 9, 17.2 mg). These are the same arms, not different arms. FDA review mapping: capsule 1/3/6/12/24/36 mg = tablet 0.8/2.5/5.5/9/14.5/17.2 mg.

Which estimand is called 'primary': Lilly topline releases present the efficacy estimand under the heading 'Primary Endpoint' / first, whereas the NEJM and Lancet abstracts, FDA review and Lilly Medical Information state the treatment-regimen estimand was primary and the efficacy estimand supportive. Efficacy-estimand values are numerically larger (e.g. ATTAIN-1 36 mg: -12.4% efficacy vs -11.2% treatment-regimen; ATTAIN-2 36 mg: -10.5% vs -9.6%).

ACHIEVE-4 p-value for MACE-4: Lancet abstract 'p<0.0001 for non-inferiority' versus Lilly release 'p = 0.336' (log-rank test). These test different hypotheses (non-inferiority vs difference); they are not interchangeable.

ACHIEVE-4 denominators within the Lancet abstract: primary outcome reported in 1358 orforglipron / 1343 insulin glargine participants, safety outcomes in 1371 / 1355, with 1371 / 1378 randomized; the abstract does not explain the difference.

ACHIEVE-4 minor descriptive discrepancies: '15 countries' (topline release text) vs '16 countries and territories' (Lancet abstract); mean baseline HbA1c 8.22% (releases) vs 8.23 (Lilly Medical Information) vs 8.2% (Lancet abstract).

Bioequivalence ratios: the applicant's analysis (FDA review Table 6.1) and FDA's own analysis (FDA Table 17) of Study GZPI differ slightly (e.g. 1 mg capsule vs 0.8 mg tablet AUC ratio 0.973 [0.9505, 0.9957] applicant vs 0.97 [0.9419, 0.9892] FDA); both conclude bioequivalence at all six dose pairs.

ATTAIN-2 publication date metadata: PubMed print PubDate field shows '2026 Dec 20' for Lancet 406(10522):2927-2944, whereas Crossref gives print publication 2025-12 and the electronic date is 2025-11-20; the PubMed year appears erroneous.

Small count discrepancies between registry and company tables: ATTAIN-1 constipation in the 6 mg arm 156/723 (ClinicalTrials.gov) vs 157 (21.7%) (Lilly Medical Information; release 21.7%); ATTAIN-1 dyspepsia 6 mg 13.0% (topline release) vs 95 (13.1%) (Lilly Medical Information).

Pooled FDA review counts of treatment discontinuation due to adverse events differ by table: FDA Table 40 (disposition reason) 5.4/8.3/10.2% vs placebo 3.2%; FDA Table 41 (adverse-event data) 5.5/8.6/10.3% vs 3.5%.
Bioequivalence study size: ClinicalTrials.gov enrollment 533 (Parts A and B) and FDA review table '533' versus 429 dosed / 398 PK-evaluable reported in the publication for the bioequivalence part.
